cards.name: Scraperboard
cards.summary: Art Strokes effect that redraws the image as a scraperboard (scratchboard) engraving: a black surface with fine scratched strokes that let the picture's own colours (Color mode) or plain white (White mode) show through, so tones become line density. Exactly how Density and Size map to the strokes is from general knowledge of the effect, not tested in this harvest.
use_for: engraved / woodcut-style portrait for a poster or book cover
vintage etched look on a product shot or label illustration
white-on-black line-art version of a photo for a one-colour print or laser engraving proof
avoid: small or low-contrast images: the fine strokes clog into black; enlarge or boost contrast first (Effects > Adjust)
you want dark lines on white paper: this is light-on-black; a pen or sketch effect such as Sketch Pad fits better
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu
scripted values beyond the dialog range: stay inside Density 1-40 and Size 1-50

params.name: ScraperMode
params.does: what the scratched strokes reveal: the image's own colours (Color) or plain white (White) for a black-and-white engraving
params.typical: Color for a tinted engraving, White for a strict two-tone print

params.name: Density
params.does: how densely the scratched strokes are laid down, i.e. how much of the black surface is cut away (more strokes reveal more of the picture)

params.name: Size
params.does: size of the individual scratch strokes; larger strokes read as a coarser, bolder engraving

pairs_with: Effects > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast/Intensity before it, so faces separate from the background
Object > Convert to Bitmap on vector art before the scripted path
a solid black or kraft-paper page background for the engraved print look
cards.scripting: On a bitmap shape s (e.g. the imported plate_photo.png): s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect "Scraperboard", "ScraperBoardEffect ScraperMode=Color,Density=20,Size=10" (signature Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect(UndoString, Command), template 'ScraperBoardEffect ScraperMode=<enum>,Density=<number>,Size=<number>'). The command format is proven on 6 other effects; this effect's string was not applied in a harvest test. ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not recognise (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed nothing), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "12be5151-7003-4b89-90d3-c8f016ddfd99" opens the effect's dialog (modal, needs a person to click OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: from the menu yes: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the Properties docker Effects stack (toggle / edit / delete, ApplyOrDeleteEffect:ScraperBoardEffect); whether the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path adds a stack entry or bakes pixels was not checked
cards.cost: moderate: a per-pixel bitmap pass at the bitmap's resolution; a 1920x1080 plate renders in seconds, very large bitmaps slow the preview

review.changes: pairs_with: 'Bitmaps > Convert to Bitmap' -> 'Object > Convert to Bitmap' (harvested path); scripting: InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, not a silent apply with current values; scripting: added that ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK on an unrecognised string

verified.note: The photo is rebuilt from dense fine scratched strokes: dark hatching over the whole plate with the picture's own colours showing through the scratches (Color mode), so tones read as stroke density, a scratchboard engraving look; the type and hairlines are scratched to rough marks.

cards.name: Sketch Pad
cards.summary: Art Strokes effect that turns the image into a pencil sketch on white paper: shading is rebuilt from hatched pencil strokes in grey graphite or in coloured pencil, with traced outlines on the edges. The exact roles of Style and Lead are from general knowledge of the effect (roughness of the hatching and pencil darkness), not tested in this harvest.
use_for: hand-drawn pencil version of a portrait or product photo for an editorial or invitation
storyboard / concept-sketch look from a reference photo
soft coloured-pencil illustration for a children's book page or greeting card
avoid: busy, low-contrast backgrounds: they turn into grey scribble; mask or simplify the background first
you want crisp ink lines instead of pencil shading: Pen & Ink (Effects > Art Strokes) suits better
LeadLabel is only the dialog's caption text, not a setting: leave it out of scripts
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: PencilType
params.does: draws with grey graphite (Graphite) or keeps the image colours as coloured pencil (Color)
params.typical: Graphite for a classic sketch, Color for an illustration feel

params.name: Style
params.does: character of the hatching, from smoother, finer shading to rougher, more visible strokes

params.name: Lead
params.does: pencil darkness / pressure: higher values lay down darker, heavier marks

params.name: Outline
params.does: how strongly the edges are traced with outline strokes; 0 leaves shading only

pairs_with: Effects > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast/Intensity before it to clean up flat, soft photos
a paper-texture bitmap fill or Wave Paper for a drawn-on-paper finish
Transparency over the original photo to blend sketch and photo
cards.scripting: On a bitmap shape s: s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect "Sketch Pad", "SketchPadEffect PencilType=Graphite,Style=30,Lead=80,Outline=50" (signature Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect(UndoString, Command), template 'SketchPadEffect PencilType=<enum>,Style=<number>,Lead=<number>,Outline=<number>'). The command format is proven on 6 other effects; this effect's string was not applied in a harvest test. ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not recognise (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed nothing), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "15a2bc1e-6f2b-46e0-850a-bf37a85b8c09" opens the effect's dialog (modal, needs a person to click OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: from the menu yes: kept in the Properties docker Effects stack (ApplyOrDeleteEffect:SketchPadEffect); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path was not checked for a stack entry vs baked pixels
cards.cost: moderate: a per-pixel bitmap pass with edge tracing; seconds on a 1920x1080 plate

review.changes: scripting: InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, not a silent apply with current values; scripting: added that ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK on an unrecognised string; avoid: named the real Pen & Ink effect

verified.note: A grey graphite pencil sketch on white: shading built from hatched pencil strokes, traced outlines on the large shapes, radial detail and dark-red blocks, colour gone (Graphite), the swatches turned into pale grey and white boxes.

cards.name: Water Marker
cards.summary: Art Strokes effect that makes the image look painted with water-based markers: the picture is broken into soft, blotchy dabs of colour with some colour shift between them. Not confirmed here: how the three variation modes arrange the dabs and exactly how Size and Color variation change the result; treat the card as a starting point.
use_for: loose, hand-coloured marker illustration from a photo for a poster or menu
playful painterly background behind headline type
quick 'drawn with markers' look for social graphics
avoid: faces and fine detail at large Size values: features dissolve into blotches; keep Size low or mask the face
you want a true wet watercolour wash: use Watercolor instead
the dialog default Size is 1, the range minimum (finest dabs); raise Size for an obvious marker look (how faint Size 1 is was not render-checked)
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: VariationMode
params.does: how the marker dabs are arranged: Default, Order (regular) or Random (scattered); exact difference not verified

params.name: Size
params.does: size of the marker dabs; larger values give a looser, more abstract result

params.name: Color variation
params.does: how much the colour of neighbouring dabs is allowed to shift away from the image colour

pairs_with: Effects > Adjust > Hue/Saturation/Lightness to push the colours more saturated before it
a clean vector outline layer on top so the shapes stay readable
Object > Convert to Bitmap on vector art before the scripted path
cards.scripting: On a bitmap shape s: s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect "Water Marker", "WaterMarkerEffect VariationMode=Random,Size=12,ColorVariation=30" (signature Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect(UndoString, Command), template 'WaterMarkerEffect VariationMode=<enum>,Size=<number>,ColorVariation=<number>'). The command format is proven on 6 other effects; this effect's string was not applied in a harvest test. ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not recognise (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed nothing), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "03871e7e-019f-4044-bdce-4bcdfcc65037" opens the effect's dialog (modal, needs a person to click OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: from the menu yes: kept in the Properties docker Effects stack (ApplyOrDeleteEffect:WaterMarkerEffect); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path was not checked for a stack entry vs baked pixels
cards.cost: moderate: a per-pixel bitmap pass; seconds on a 1920x1080 plate, slower as Size grows

review.changes: pairs_with: 'Bitmaps > Convert to Bitmap' -> 'Object > Convert to Bitmap' (harvested path); scripting: InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, not a silent apply with current values; scripting: added that ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK on an unrecognised string; Size 1 'barely changes / nearly invisible' was an untested claim: reworded as the range minimum, not render-checked

verified.note: The plate is broken into soft, blotchy dabs of colour like water-based marker, with visible colour shifts between dabs (Random variation), the large shapes and stripes still readable, the swatches and type dabbed.

cards.name: Watercolor
cards.summary: Art Strokes effect that repaints the image as a watercolour: detail dissolves into soft washes of colour that bleed into each other, with a grainy paper texture. Brush size, Water amount and Bleed control how loose the washes are, Granulation the paper grain and Brightness the overall lightness.
use_for: painted watercolour version of a travel or event photo for an invitation or poster
soft artistic background plate behind type
hand-painted feel for wedding stationery, menus and greeting cards
avoid: small text or logos inside the image: they smear; apply the effect to the photo only and keep type as vector on top
high Water amount plus high Bleed on a photo that is already soft (like the PGD plate) can turn into mush; lower Bleed if subjects disappear
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu
scripted values beyond the dialog range: stay inside Brush size 1-10 and 1-100 for the others

params.name: Brush size
params.does: size of the paint strokes; larger brushes lose more detail

params.name: Granulation
params.does: graininess of the paper / pigment texture showing through the washes

params.name: Water amount
params.does: how wet the brush is: more water gives softer, more diluted, flowing colour

params.name: Bleed
params.does: how far colours run into neighbouring areas

params.name: Brightness
params.does: overall lightness of the painted result

pairs_with: Effects > Adjust > Hue/Saturation/Lightness to lift the colours after the wash
a paper-texture bitmap fill under a slightly transparent result
vector type and line art on top so the important edges stay crisp
cards.scripting: On a bitmap shape s: s.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect "Watercolor", "WatercolorEffect BrushSize=5,Granulation=60,WaterAmount=70,Bleed=55,Brightness=30" (signature Shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect(UndoString, Command), template 'WatercolorEffect BrushSize=<number>,Granulation=<number>,WaterAmount=<number>,Bleed=<number>,Brightness=<number>'). The command format is proven on 6 other effects; this effect's string was not applied in a harvest test. ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not recognise (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed nothing), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "3281ba98-f440-471f-a66a-8f093d2058be" opens the effect's dialog (modal, needs a person to click OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: from the menu yes: kept in the Properties docker Effects stack (ApplyOrDeleteEffect:WatercolorEffect); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path was not checked for a stack entry vs baked pixels
cards.cost: moderate to heavy: a multi-pass bitmap simulation; a few seconds on a 1920x1080 plate, noticeably slower with large Brush size

review.changes: scripting: InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, not a silent apply with current values; scripting: added that ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK on an unrecognised string

verified.note: The photo dissolves into soft, bleeding washes on a light paper: detail is lost, the dark areas become blotchy grey-green pools, the colours spread past their edges and the whole frame is much lighter (Brightness 30; mean 199 vs 133), a loose watercolour look.

cards.name: Wave Paper
cards.summary: Art Strokes effect that makes the image look painted on rough, textured paper, overlaying a fine wavy paper grain on the picture, in colour or reduced to black and white. Brush pressure sets how strongly the texture shows; the exact texture pattern is from general knowledge of the effect and not verified in this harvest. On the 2026-10 gallery render (Pressure 16, Color mode) the texture was a fine grain and the colours faded strongly toward pastel (the red swatch went pale pink, mid grey 128 to 176).
use_for: giving a flat photo or render a printed-on-paper, hand-made finish
textured backgrounds for posters, certificates and packaging mock-ups
black-and-white textured treatment of a photo for a retro print look (Black and White mode)
avoid: fine text or thin lines inside the bitmap: the texture breaks them up; keep type as vector on top
you need a specific texture (canvas, brick, burlap): use a bitmap pattern fill or a dedicated texture effect instead
a ColorMode value with spaces ('Black and White') may need quoting in the scripted command string; that encoding was not tested
the scripted path works only on a bitmap shape (Shape.Bitmap); convert vector objects to a bitmap first or apply from the menu

params.name: Brush pressure
params.does: strength of the paper texture over the image; low values are subtle, high values dominate

params.name: ColorMode
params.does: keeps the image colours (Color) or renders the result in black and white (Black and White)

pairs_with: Sketch Pad or Watercolor before it for a drawn / painted on paper result
Effects > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast/Intensity to recover contrast after the texture
Object > Convert to Bitmap on vector art before the scripted path

The command format is proven on 6 other effects; this effect's string was not applied in a harvest test. ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK even for a string it does not recognise (the harvest's Pixelate and Invert strings changed nothing), so compare the pixels before and after. Menu route: Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "bdc5d812-24de-4136-8a91-e4689f4918f8" opens the effect's dialog (modal, needs a person to click OK), so it is not an unattended route.
cards.non_destructive: from the menu yes: kept in the Properties docker Effects stack (ApplyOrDeleteEffect:WavePaperEffect); the scripted Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect path was not checked for a stack entry vs baked pixels
cards.cost: light to moderate: a single texture pass over the bitmap; quick on a 1920x1080 plate

review.changes: pairs_with: 'Bitmaps > Convert to Bitmap' -> 'Object > Convert to Bitmap' (harvested path); scripting: InvokeItem opens the modal dialog, not a silent apply with current values; scripting: added that ApplyBitmapEffect returns OK on an unrecognised string

verified.note: A fine grainy paper texture lies over the whole plate (Pressure 16, Color mode), and the colours fade strongly toward pastel (red swatch 232,32,42 -> 230,210,211, mid grey 128 -> 176), a printed-on-rough-paper look; the fading is now stated in the summary.
